key_concepts: The IAU classifies non-planet, non-moon solar system objects as small solar system bodies
Dwarf planets orbit the Sun and are spherical but have not cleared their orbital neighborh
Pluto, Eris, and Ceres are dwarf planets; Eris is the largest and Ceres the smallest.
Asteroids are rocky bodies, mostly found in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
Jupiter's gravity likely prevented a planet from forming in the asteroid belt.
Comets are icy bodies of dust, rock, frozen water, methane, and ammonia.
A comet near the Sun forms a coma and dust and ion tails that point away from the Sun.
Halley's comet orbits the Sun about every 76 years and was last seen in 1986.
The Oort Cloud is a distant cloud of comets beyond Pluto's orbit.
